entries.note: Colours, microui metrics, the font pixel size and the line height come from orchestrator/native/theme.h, which `python3 tools/design.py generate` derives from design/tokens.json; the same tokens feed the Claude Design preview cards. Edit the tokens and regenerate, never the header: `tools/design.py check` rejects a stale header and any mu_color/vterm_color_rgb literal outside the palette. Applying upstream microui's default slots explicitly here is behaviour-neutral (identical values) and makes every slot designable. Every owned native source uses RE_COLOR_* through common.h; `check` fails on any numeric colour literal, so a new colour starts as a token.

The list is flushed exactly once per frame by whichever of re_draw_snapshot or re_draw_end runs first, because main.c snapshots before presenting. Commands execute in append order with the same adapter calls the former immediate-mode path issued; that is what keeps native snapshots byte-identical across the contract change (spec 067). Views must append to the list, never draw directly, and anything above the list must not name graphics-API rendering symbols (tools/design.py check enforces it).

`seam-opengl`, `seam-vulkan` and `seam-metal` are not graphics APIs and are not meant to survive. They exist so each copy of the draw list's new path through `packs/gpu` can be selected beside the hand-written backend it replaces and judged against it by `native-render.spec.mjs` — which they are, to 0 differing pixels across all 15 cross-backend pairs — **before** any of those backends is deleted.

What replaces them (spec 126 decision 3, owner-confirmed): `opengl`, `metal` and `vulkan` dispatch straight into the prefixed copies. `--renderer` stays a runtime switch, the pack stays compile-time selected so D14b's zero indirection holds for the games it serves, and these branches go together with `backend_gl.c`, `backend_metal.m`, `backend_vk.c` and `backend_sdl.c`. All three exist now.
